import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and clean style for the visualization
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a multi-dimensional scatter plot (bubble chart)
# x-axis: price_usd
# y-axis: megapixels
# hue (color): brand
# size: weight_grams
# style (marker): body_type
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    hue='brand',
    size='weight_grams',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(200, 2000),  # Control the range of bubble sizes
    palette='viridis',
    ax=ax,
    edgecolor='black',
    alpha=0.75,
    legend='full'
)

# Enhance the plot with titles and labels for clarity
fig.suptitle("Camera Feature Comparison", fontsize=24, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title("Price vs. Megapixels, Sized by Weight", fontsize=16, pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel("Price (USD)", fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel("Megapixels (MP)", fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Add annotations for each data point to provide specific details
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.text(
        row['price_usd'] + 60,  # Offset text for better readability
        row['megapixels'],
        f"{row['brand']} ({row['model_year']})\n{row['sensor_type']}",
        fontsize=11,
        ha='left',
        va='center',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec="gray", lw=0.5, alpha=0.7)
    )

# Format the x-axis to show dollar signs and commas
ax.get_xaxis().set_major_formatter(
    plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x:,.0f}')
)

# Improve the legend by placing it outside the main plot area
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Manually adjust labels for clarity
brand_idx = labels.index('brand')
body_type_idx = labels.index('body_type')
weight_idx = labels.index('weight_grams')
labels[brand_idx] = 'Brand'
labels[body_type_idx] = 'Body Type'
labels[weight_idx] = 'Weight (grams)'

ax.legend(
    handles,
    labels,
    title="Legend",
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.04, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.
)

# Ensure the layout is tight to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.83, 0.95]) # Adjust rect for suptitle and legend

# Save the resulting visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
